brief: UBS's monthly Macro Equity Navigator argues AI equity positioning has turned favorably asymmetric: the crowding gap between its AI Winners and Ex-AI 400 baskets has unwound back to February levels, and the scale of the derating now prices too pessimistic an AI outlook, tilting risk-reward higher even as sentiment stays fragile. Within AI, money has rotated into Hyperscalers (stronger cash flow, cleaner balance sheets, existing compute) and away from Neoclouds, which still sits at the leverage/buildout-risk end, making Hyperscalers the preferred defensive AI exposure. Because the broader market's breadth expansion has depended on AI weakness, pockets like Consumer Staples (still-poor earnings revisions) are vulnerable to a reversal. Strategist Keith Parker's top 2027 trade is XLV over XLP. China is drawing renewed diversifier interest, but CSI 300 earnings revisions versus the S&P 500 sit at multi-year lows, and recovery needs that to turn plus stronger policy support and property stabilization. Separately, European equities (Stoxx 600) are making new highs versus the S&P 500, aided by only ~11% AI exposure, a still-constructive view on European Banks despite a softer Q3, an Energy-to-Metals rotation as Brent de-risks, and strength in UK Domestics after the PM change and a steady Budget.
